It should be obvious that cutting interest rates to the bone in an effort to spur spending is simply an inept application of failed Keynesian economics. If banks can be issued currency at a near-zero rate, then buy govt bonds at rates higher than that, it's going to create /exactly/ this problem. There's simply no reason to lend when banks can turn a near-zero risk profit on volume by sitting on govt bonds. Removing govt from setting prime interest rates would solve this velocity of money problem in a heartbeat for obvious reasons.

TLDR: If you could borrow money from the govt at ~0%, then invest in govt bonds at a > 0% interest rate, why would you do anythings other than borrow billions and turn a passive profit at "no" risk?
